question: Is our Occ3D-nuScenes number faithfully comparable to OccAny's published 23.55%?
answer: The measurement is faithful; the comparison is not like-for-like until three asymmetries are named, and all three run against us.

metric.how: OccAny's own SSCMetrics.get_score_completion (occany/metrics/ssc.py) was run on 193 of our real Occ3D predictions and compared with our counting
metric.result: byte-identical TP/FP/FN on every clip (exact agreement = True)

verified_identical.grid: 200x200x16 @ 0.4 m, origin (-40,-40,-1), ego frame of the target sample
verified_identical.masks: mask_camera applied -> 255; mask_lidar NOT applied; voxel_label[:100,:,:] = 255 (the rear half, single-camera setting). Our gate6/targets.py does the same three operations in the same order.
verified_identical.occupied_free: class 17 = free, 255 = ignore and excluded from TP/FP/FN by both
verified_identical.split_and_camera: Occ3D-nuScenes official val, 150 scenes, CAM_FRONT only

sample_subset.occany: ~4800 (every frame with 8 more ahead of it); 6019 val frames carry a GT file

representativeness_check.verdict: our subsample is representative; pooled IoU is comparable in expectation

post_processing.finding: sh/compute_metric.sh sets USE_MAJORITY_POOLING=1 by default and sh/exp_lists/metric_occany.sh EXP_ID 2 (nuScenes 5frames geometry) passes --geometry_only $MAJORITY_POOLING_ARG
post_processing.consequence: the published 23.55% is POST-PROCESSED with apply_majority_pooling in geometry-only mode, whose default use_dilation=True is a 3x3x3 max-pool (a one-voxel dilation), while our 30.89% is raw

temporal_direction.occany: target is the FIRST frame; the other four run forward at interval 2 (~1.0 s apart, ~4 s of future observation of the target region)
temporal_direction.ours_primary: five frames ENDING at the target, no future observation at all

asymmetries_against_us.target_domain_training: OccAny trains on nuScenes; our completion module never saw it
asymmetries_against_us.threshold_tuning: OccAny sets --recon_threshold/--gen_threshold per dataset (nuScenes 1.1, KITTI 2.5); our threshold was frozen on KITTI-360 validation before Occ3D was opened

most_defensible_like_for_like.description: matched temporal sampling (target-first forward), matched post-processing (OccAny max-pool), OccAny's evaluator, identical grid/masks/split
most_defensible_like_for_like.caveat: still favours OccAny on training data and threshold tuning

as_reported_in_report_md.note: conservative for us: raw vs pooled

semantickitti_for_contrast.note: the conclusion there is unchanged by any of this: we are ~half of OccAny
